text: But knowing the three shapes is not the same as knowing which one to reach for. So let me give you the honest answer for each, because they are genuinely good at different things, and nobody tells you this part.

Reach for the I D E when you want to see what is happening. Everything is visible. The files on the left, the code in the middle, the agent on the right. You can watch a change land, scroll the difference, and undo it. That makes it the right place to start, and the right place to be whenever you are unsure.

Reach for the plugin when the editor is not the point. You already have your setup, your extensions, your keyboard shortcuts, and you do not want to move house just to get an agent. Bolt it on. This is also, very often, the one your employer has already paid for, which settles the argument.

And reach for the command line when you want to hand over real work. It sounds backwards, because it is the least friendly of the three. But a terminal is trivially easy to automate, to script, to run several of at once, and to leave running for an hour while you do something else. That is why the professionals live there, and it is why weeks two and three do too.
Now here is the part that matters more than any of that. The shape is the chassis. The model underneath is the engine. And the engine is what decides whether the thing you get back is any good.

You can run a weak model inside a beautiful I D E and get nonsense. You can run a frontier model in an ugly terminal and get something excellent. So when you are choosing, and especially when you are deciding what to pay for, spend the money on the model, not on the wrapper. We will come back to this properly, with numbers, tomorrow.

And one last piece of advice about all these names. The brands on this list will change. Some of them will be gone in a year, and there will be several that do not exist yet. But the three shapes will not change. An application, an add on, or a terminal. Anchor on the shapes, and every new tool that appears is just a new example of something you already understand.
